solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Message received, seeing headline about leading track runner

parts.note: radio operators say Roger to confirm a message has been received

indicators.note: about means going around, so the headline wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a banner is a newspaper headline running across the page
leading means first, written 1ST and read as IST

explanation.surface: A radio operator acknowledges a message, having seen a front-page story about a champion runner.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often write 'first' as the ordinal 1ST and read the digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Roger Bannister was the British athlete who first ran a mile in under four minutes, in 1954.

clue.text: Referee begins to develop, in command when dismissing wingers

indicators.note: in places the budding piece inside the trimmed word
wingers are the letters at each side, so the outer letters of command are dropped

parts.note: a plant that buds begins to develop its flowers

explanation.surface: A football referee starts to grow into the job, taking charge once the wide players are sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Referee' and 'wingers' paint a football match; wingers here are simply the end letters of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official who arbitrates complaints, acting as an impartial referee between public and institution.

clue.text: Football team, one down, start to tire in time that's added on

indicators.note: in places the team-and-letter piece inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: one is the letter I, and down means it is lost from the team

parts.note: a football side is an eleven, written in Roman numerals as XI

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A football side, one player short, begins to tire during stoppage time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one down' means the letter for one is lost; a football eleven in Roman numerals is the usual source.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extra is additional, supplementing what was already there.

clue.text: Just touring, Prince of Wales left out European city

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the first word encircles the other piece

parts.note: just, as in 'just a moment', can mean but ('but a moment')

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is removed from the name

parts.note: Charles was Prince of Wales for decades before becoming king

explanation.surface: Simply going on tour, the heir to the throne skipped a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: When this puzzle appeared, the Prince of Wales was Charles, now king.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital of Romania, a city in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Stocking some vinyl online

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shop is selling vinyl records over the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings are often made of a synthetic fibre, so the fabric name stands for the hosiery itself.

clue.text: Unable to drop off Monica at work under current partnership

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this piece follows the earlier ones

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
in bridge, North and South form a partnership, NS

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters are busy being rearranged

explanation.surface: Monica is busy in the office beneath a modern business partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as two partnerships, North-South and East-West, hence the two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who suffers from insomnia cannot fall asleep at night.

clue.text: Having removed top, highlight hair

indicators.note: top is the first letter in a down entry, so that opening letter is taken off

parts.note: to highlight a point is to stress it

explanation.surface: After taking off a hat, someone shows off highlights in their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having removed top' takes S off STRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock or long strand of hair.

clue.text: Old Egyptian repeatedly outside in elements, has woolly thing on

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means one piece sits above the rest

parts.note: a ram is a fleecy male sheep

indicators.note: repeatedly says the picked letters are taken twice
outside picks the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A mummified pharaoh, wrapped in layers again and again, wears a woolly garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' of ELEMENTS gives ES; 'repeatedly' doubles it to ESES, with RAM placed 'on' top.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameses was the name of several pharaohs of ancient Egypt, notably Rameses II.

clue.text: Piece of game from party doctor eats at home

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: eats means the doctor takes the next piece inside

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A doctor at a party eats in, and the game pieces come out.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is a standard crossword doctor alongside DR, GP and MB.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is one of the rectangular tiles used to play the game of dominoes.

clue.text: Cycle dash past centre of York

indicators.note: past means the next piece comes after the earlier one
centre of takes the middle letters of the place name

parts.note: a dash of something is a small bit of it

explanation.surface: A cyclist makes a quick dash past the middle of York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' York gives OR, and BIT goes 'past' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is one complete revolution, a cycle around a central body.

clue.text: Stadium officer succeeded in moving mouse

parts.note: COL abbreviates colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the rearranged word
moving suggests the letters are shifted about

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: An officer has managed to shift a mouse out of the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns MOUSE into OSEUM and 'in' places S inside it, giving OSSEUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum is the great amphitheatre of ancient Rome, and the word now names any large stadium.

clue.text: State aid's written about in local article

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the pub and article

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn

indicators.note: written about means the word aid is set down the wrong way round

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A report on state funding appears in the regional press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local article' suggests a newspaper piece, but a 'local' is a neighbourhood pub in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Extremely naive individual in disarray finds ancient deity

indicators.note: extremely picks the letters at the extremes, the first and last
in places the single letter inside the muddle

parts.note: a mess is a state of disarray
I, the Roman one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: An extremely innocent person, flustered, stumbles upon an old god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarray' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, punishing hubris.

clue.text: Sound of trombone perhaps lacking a sparkle

indicators.note: lacking means the letter that follows is removed

parts.note: oompah imitates the deep rhythmic sound of brass instruments such as the trombone

explanation.surface: A trombone's tone is flat and lacks any spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' takes one A out of OOMPAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is vitality or energy, the sparkle that makes something lively.

clue.text: The masses head into Nicosia regularly on early part of holiday

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means a piece sits on top of the one before

parts.note: the early part of the word holiday is its opening two letters

indicators.note: into means the head goes inside the selected letters
regularly picks every other letter of the city name

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in poll tax

explanation.surface: Crowds head into Nicosia at the start of the holiday season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a verb but is the noun, in its old sense kept in 'poll tax' and 'opinion poll'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi, Greek for 'the many', is used for ordinary people, the common crowd.

clue.text: Futility of record company head retaining personal trainer

indicators.note: retaining means the company name holds the next piece inside

parts.note: EMI is a well-known British record company
PT stands for physical training, and a personal trainer
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A record label boss keeps on a personal trainer, to no great purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not the boss of the company but a headland, a common element in Scottish place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptiness is a lack of meaning or purpose, which is what futility describes.

clue.text: Training new China correspondent

parts.note: PE is physical education, training at school
in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so a china is a friend

explanation.surface: A new teaching assignment in China is being arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, i.e. friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend is a person you write letters to regularly, so they are a correspondent.

clue.text: Skinny latte, finally, Scotsman on a diet ordered

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the coffee

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Scotsman on a diet ordered a skinny latte.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E from LATTE; 'ordered' turns A DIET into IATED.
explanation.definitionFit: An emaciated person is extremely thin, wasted by hunger or illness.

clue.text: Canine character runs into container twice

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
into gives the letters IN

indicators.note: twice says the container appears two times

parts.note: a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: A dog runs into a container, then does it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Rin Tin Tin was a German shepherd dog who starred in Hollywood films and television.

clue.text: Bull and Ram's Head — where booze's served in the middle

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in places the drinking venue inside the centre

parts.note: a hub is the centre or middle of something
a bar is where drinks are served

explanation.surface: The Bull and the Ram's Head sound like pubs with drinks served right in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' and 'Ram's Head' look like pub names, but Bull is the definition: slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for nonsense, and rhubarb is British slang for nonsensical talk.

clue.text: Stroke fawn

definitions.meaning: to fawn is to grovel and flatter obsequiously

explanation.definitionFit: The front swimming stroke shares a name with the verb for obsequious grovelling.

clue.text: When delivering inflatable mattress, keep quiet

indicators.note: delivering a word means speaking it, so it is judged by its spoken form

parts.note: a Lilo is a brand of air bed used on beaches

explanation.surface: Bringing a blow-up mattress, someone is told to keep the noise down.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lilo is a British brand of inflatable mattress for beach or pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to keep out of sight and quiet, avoiding attention.

clue.text: Free Kenyan leader joining two alliances

indicators.note: joining means the leader is attached to the alliances

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is one alliance
a bloc is a second alliance of nations

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Kenyan leader is released after joining two international groupings.
explanation.definitionFit: To unblock is to clear an obstruction and let things move freely.

clue.text: Launched appeal with article

parts.note: to beg is to appeal earnestly
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A charity launched an appeal with a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Launched, as in started something off, means commenced.

clue.text: Tree-dweller sadly curtailed after decisive blow

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word following the blow

parts.note: KO, a knockout, is the decisive blow in boxing

indicators.note: curtailed means having the tail, the final letter, cut off

parts.note: alas is said sadly, expressing grief

explanation.surface: A tree-climbing animal, sadly cut short after a knockout blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the last letter of ALAS, leaving ALA.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is an Australian marsupial that lives in eucalyptus trees.

clue.text: Pause, always taking in peaks westwards

indicators.note: westwards in an across clue means read from right to left
taking in means the poetic word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
tips are peaks or tops

explanation.surface: Someone stops for a moment, forever gazing at the mountain peaks to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' gives ETIPSER, and 'westwards' turns it right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or interval of rest from something difficult.

clue.text: Refuse from the outset to sign document

indicators.note: from the outset means only the very first letter is used

parts.note: a will is a legal document

explanation.surface: Someone refuses from the start to sign a legal document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: kitchen scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill is kitchen waste fed to pigs, a kind of rubbish.

clue.text: On a spree, glance Jackie regularly nibbling sweet stuff

indicators.note: on a spree suggests wild behaviour, so the letters are scrambled
regularly picks every second letter of the name

explanation.surface: Out on the town, Jackie keeps snacking on cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a spree' turns GLANCE into ANGELC; 'regularly' gives AKE from JACKIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a very light sponge cake, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Drinker, at last inside, enthusiastic about bars opening

indicators.note: inside means the letter goes within the next piece

parts.note: to be into something is to be enthusiastic about it

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drinker finally inside a pub is keen on the bars as they open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' are bars of music here, and 'opening' is the definition; INTO surrounds R.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music.

clue.text: Couple on the run from city with Diane crossed British river

parts.note: Bonn is a German city, formerly West Germany's capital

indicators.note: crossed means mixed up, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the Clyde is the river that flows through Glasgow

explanation.surface: A pair flee a city with Diane, crossing a British river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed' turns DIANE into IEAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were the notorious American outlaw pair of the 1930s.
